words.sense: Wrongdoing or illegal action by a person exercising public office or entrusted authority
misconceptions: Public-office abuse and negligent expert service are interchangeable

words.sense: Improper or negligent conduct in a professional service role
misconceptions: Public-office abuse and negligent expert service are interchangeable

semantic_axes.description: Whether the scene turns on capacity of actor.
Whether the scene turns on kind of breach.

edges.boundary_rule: Malfeasance abuses official authority or public trust; malpractice breaches standards of professional care or skill.

misconceptions.M3: Public-office abuse and negligent expert service are interchangeable

chains.frame: Which word best describes Zara’s conduct as an elected council member?

beats.text: Zara used her council authority to send public repair money to her own account.
beats.reason: The detail about misuse of public office supports malfeasance more strongly than malpractice.

beats.text: Investigators found she had personally approved the transfer after being told it violated council rules.
beats.reason: The detail about knowingly authorized diversion supports malfeasance more strongly than malpractice.

chains.feedback_short: Knowingly authorized diversion leaves malfeasance the better fit.
chains.feedback_deep: The first clue is misuse of public office. The later clue is knowingly authorized diversion; that strengthens or preserves the same classification. Malfeasance abuses official authority or public trust; malpractice breaches standards of professional care or skill.
chains.contrast_rule: Malfeasance betrays entrusted authority; malpractice breaches professional care.

hints.attention: Check the person’s authority and the duty that was breached.
hints.axis: Whether the scene turns on capacity of actor.
hints.contrast: Malfeasance betrays entrusted authority; malpractice breaches professional care.
